27-10-2023

Introduction:
 started the channel PTT2019 on telegram in his early days of CSE
Preparation. Since then, this channel has become an essential component of everyone’s CSE
journey. The idea is simple, community members send their individual interview transcript
to the admins, which are then posted on our channel. This was started when transcripts were
sold on various channels and ORN market and due to community efforts only this stands
demonetised today.
This pdf is just the plain compilation of all the Interview
Transcripts of the session 2022-23 which were posted on our channel. This compilation is
not that organized due to paucity of time.
This compilation is based on the initial works done by a
user Vijay and I have just added few other transcripts in his pdf.
Lastly this was possible only because community (the members who appeared for interview
sent us their transcripts) came forward and hence this is dedicated to the entire CSE family.
I humbly request to those who will benefit from this pdf and are going to appear for CSPT2023, please send us your transcripts on the admin handles mentioned in the description of
our telegram channel (ptt2019).
Best Wishes,
Kaptaan and Team PTT

Other members looked satisfied, they were nodding and smiling.

Utility of mocks:
Don't take them seriously (EASIER SAID THAN DONE). Just look at the overall feedback and areas to
improve. I gave a hell lot of mocks, some were decent, some were horrible and some very factual.
This interview at UPSC was very relaxed. Luckily I wasn't asked any difficult sociology/GS/graduation
questions or any random current affairs question. In fact, I prepared so much for Uttarakhand that I

can clear UKPCS now! 😅 But they didn't ask anything from Uttarakhand. That doesn't mean we
should not prepare, it's just that you've to be ready for everything. I was told that teaching, NCC,
blood donation are very generic things and they won't ask. But you can see so many questions were
asked. So don't leave any part of DAF.

All the best! See you in LBSNAA.

Remarks: Overall 80% question from DAF. Soni sir was smiling and all the member's were very
cordial. Fear in real interview was only 20% of mocks. Real interview is all together a different game. I
am not sure what my marks would be but I enjoyed the entire interview. Initially I was little nervous
but by 10 min later, only i was speaking and rest were listening and observing me very closely. Just go
and enjoy the process. What I felt was not knowledge but what you really are would come to your
rescue in the final interview. I was not able to revise so much content which I scrambled during
interview preparation. But what helped me answering was what I really felt. I am done with this
years cycle. I want to say to all BEST OF LUCK. Don't run after so much content - only 2 things needed
= your DAF and your BROAD UNDERSTANDING. Rest you can deny if you really don't know. That way
you can manage 60-70% of your interview nicely.

My mocks: Vision IAS, NEXTIAS, Vajirao and Reddy, RaoIAS and one to one with many including
Ravindran sir
Observation of mocks: you can give mocks but don't run after many. Choose few and focus on your
own core strength. All institutes are equally good and equally bad. They on the one hand help you in
giving simulator environment but on the other hand break your own confidence like RaosIAS did with
me. Give 4,5,6 mocks and I think you can develop your confidence within this much feeding.
That's all from my interview. Best of luck to all.

demand of the question. I liberally said 'I don't know' for some questions and they hinted me and

Your experience in interview- The board was very cordial. They will try to trap us or pressurize us
with tricky questions but the essence is to remain calm and composed. (Please remember it is a test
of personality and not of knowledge. Questions are asked to get out your personality in pressure
conditions. So the way one answers is more important. And there is no harm in saying sorry if you
don't know the answer, but DO NOT BLUFF/FAKE/IMPRESS/SHOW-OFF.

questions/issues/opinions, especially based on any keywords in our answers to previous questions.

and in OnlyIAS. Both were really outstanding. They revealed my fault lines and gave me really very
valuable feedback to work upon. And I believe 80% of the interview came from these mocks, my
subsequent preparations and one-to-one talk with my senior civil servant friends and my friend-cummentor.

May I come in, sir

Answered (don't ask what, because I can't remember kya bola tha, but I made some sense, that's for

Chair - Okay, Tell me whether you are following the international events these days?

Me - Yes sir, I am slightly aware
about the geopolitics of the day...

Then what followed was a general discussion and questions/ counter questions on geopolitical
events like...

Whether we are going to see a cold war 2.0 , similar to the cold war..? (few counter questions)
Is India right in maintaining the doctrine of strategic autonomy, or should we change our policy and
join any faction (based on the last discussion around geopolitical uncertainties and negative
headwinds)??? This was followed by 2–3 counter questions..

I said that considering the present scenario of India, where we are dependent on US, RUSSIA AND
CHINA, we can't afford to join any block... It will not be in our interest in larger term...

Chair - China is very adamant in capturing Taiwan... It's most likely bound to happen... This gives us a
breathing space on LAC... What's your opinion, should we stop bothering about security situation on
LAC for now and focus our energy elsewhere?

(I said NO, as we are not sure about the movements of china, and ignoring the LAC security would
not be a good idea..)
Few questions about make in India defence and atmanirbhar bharat(mostly centered around
defence).

The interrogation of Shukla sir must have lasted 10–15 minutes at least, overall I felt satisfied with
my answers and wore a pleasant and enthusiastic smile throughout...
Then he passed on to M1 (male).

M1 -

I would want you to continue on the Pakistan angle... Tell me what are the causes of present crisis in

What is the similarity between Pakistan and Sri Lanka crisis? (I could have done better, but I decided
to cut it short when I knew I was about to beat around the bush)

Tell me what are the issues for regions around India and what sort of challenge does it pose to us..(I
think I answered it quite decently, covering all the countries and the challenges that we face, he
looked pretty satisfied).

Few more counter questions based on my answers.
Baton is now passed to M2( another gentleman)

M2

So you have worked as a customer service executive in a company, for some time?
Yes sir

So, tell me... There is a perception among the people that government officers are not working and
not people friendly... They are marred with so much negativity? How will you reduce this perception?
Me - answered (my answers revolved around a citizen charter, staff training, formal and informal
grievance redressal via social media etc)
Bihar is one of the poorest state of India in terms of per capita income, and it is also a state with
lowest literacy... So , do you think that there's any linkages between low literacy and low per capita
income?

Me - “Yes sir( then proceeded with problems in school system like infra shortage, teacher training
and absenteeism, low employability of students and resultant lack of employment Avenues in job
market where skilled labour is required and hence only the menial jobs are left for the people.)”
How would you tackle the problem of teacher absenteeism in schools of Bihar?

Me - answered (infrastructure like biometric attendance, CCTV etc), but member wasn't pleased as
he said that there is financial crunch in government and they are unlikely to provide for CCTV or
computers or biometric attendance monitoring systems...he asked me to give a cheaper solution...

Me - a mechanism of anonymous complaint by peers and students can be created and it can be
coupled with surprise visits, teacher training etc...
Okay.
Now came M3 (another gentleman).

M3

The government of India spends billions of dollars in terms of giving free food grains to crores of
people in India.... It creates a huge financial burden on the exchequer and a lot of resources are
diverted in this.. do you think India should continue giving the food grains to so many people?

Yes sir, I am of the opinion that there's still a huge chunk of below the threshold poverty who can
barely afford to get 2 square meals a day... This food distribution is not only ensuring their food
security and curbing hunger, but even from an economic point of view, its a good capital investment,
in the human resources of India....

The inequality index released by the global organisations put india behind so many countries like
Russia and all... Are you aware about it?

Me - yes sir I am aware about the degree of inequality that India has, but I'm unsure about the exact
rank of India...
No problem, just tell me whether there is inequality in India in terms of resources availablity?

Yes sir, as per the Oxfam report, the top 1 percent of people have access to almost 50 percent of the
resources and the bottom 70 percent of the people thrive on a mere 30 percent...

What is your opinion? Do you think this degree of inequality is harmful to us as a country and a
society?

Me - yes sir, this stark inequality is harmful for us... We can not strive for perfect equality as it will
disincentivise merit and talent , but such stark inequality is the breeding ground for almost all the
problems and crimes that we as a society face...

How do you suggest we bring down this inequality? What you would do if given the task of reducing
inequality?

Me - answered on bookish line like guaranteed minimum wages like mgnrega, universal health
Coverage, UBI for the weakest and vulnerable, quality education as per the demands of the job
market etc...
No counter questions here..

Me - ICDS , MDM, food distribution program , targeting the young age group especially children as

Do you think it's possible to bring a change in behaviour of people?

Chairman sir - your interview is over, you may leave now..

Now, coming to the utility of mocks - i gave around 10 mocks this year including group mocks and
one to one sessions...

Giving mocks is a fun exercise and somewhat helpful in bringing small yet significant changes in our
personality... It also helps us face senior people and frame the answers... Baki, Don't expect a
repeatetion of questions in actual mock (there can be some repeated questions, but that doesn't
make a difference).

My overall verdict - “Ab verdict to Shukla sir denge Bhai, hamari kya aukaat...”

I did the best that I could and I am pretty satisfied with the experience... If I get marks, that's very
good... If I don't, then that's my fate, what can we do? Nothing to be precise...
